messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PAGER fired -> prometheus.scrape.failure (rule: prom_scrape_failures_high). Target: prometheus-exporter (monitoring).
incident-bot: Alert details: 4xx/429 rate from exporter, >50% scrape failures over 5m. Runbook: <https://redwood.runbooks/prom-scrape-failures>.
maya: acked. I'm on it.
maya: quick status: seeing ~60% scrape failures across prod exporters, a bunch of 429s in exporter logs. Suspect upstream pull/throttling.
maya: running checks now:
```bash
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=prometheus-exporter -o wide
# prometheus-exporter-0   1/1 Running   0       5m
# prometheus-exporter-1   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   3   4m
```
maya: logs show repeated 429s from the backend storage tier: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z exporter.go:412 WARNING: scrape failed: status=429 Too Many Requests, retry after 10s
```
jasper: thanks. is this correlated with log-ingest kafka backlog? last time exporter throttled when downstream was overloaded.
carlos: checking consumers now. grabbing kafka lag for metrics-consumer-prod...
carlos: ```
# kafka-consumer-lag --group metrics-consumer-prod --topic metrics._prom_scrapes
lag: 128,432 messages
consumer-rate: 6k msg/s
```
jasper: that's high. can confirm backlog + exporter 429s -> likely downstream write throttling. ops_lead: please annotate customer impact. any customer-facing errors?
maya: quick sweep of HTTP 5xx on API indicates no direct 5xx spikes, but monitoring dashboards missing metrics for a few tenants (metrics not scraped). Customer impact: some dashboards will show stale data, alerting may be delayed. marking P2 but could go P1 if backlog persists >1h.
incident-bot: Auto-escalation: alert still active after 5m, escalating to on-call-sre-2 and ops_lead.
ops_lead: I'm on rotation OL. Plan: 1) throttle scrape rate, 2) restart exporter pod(s) to clear transient state, 3) temporarily scale up write buffer/replicas if infra allows.
maya: applying quick mitigations: reducing scrape concurrency in prometheus config for prod targets (patching config map) and will restart the failing exporter pod.
maya: ```bash
kubectl -n monitoring patch cm prometheus-scrape-config -p '{"data":{"scrape_interval":"15s","concurrency":"4"}}'
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/prometheus-exporter
```
jasper: while that runs, I can provision a short-lived extra replica on write-tier (if cloud quota ok) and open a ticket with infra to increase ingestion buffer. carlos can you trigger a consumer rebalance?
carlos: rebalance started. opened PD incident: PD-INC-98231 and linked to this thread. pinging GCP support for throttling evidence.
customer-ops: flagging customer comms: creating a short status note: "Some customers may see stale metrics dashboards — investigating, mitigation in progress." Will post on status.redwood.ai if impact broadens.
maya: exporter restart rolled, one pod still cycling but new pod is up. logs now show few 429s but falling.
maya: post-restart checks:
```bash
# sample metric: prom_scrape_success_ratio{job="exporter-prod"}
before: 0.38
after: 0.92
# kafka lag:
lag: 21,400 messages (decreasing)
```
jasper: nice. keep an eye on lag drop rate. if it plateaus, we need to scale write-tier.
ops_lead: agreed. for now hold on escalation. carlos please coordinate infra ticket and share ETA.
carlos: infra ticket created (INF-2045). initial response ETA 30m. PR to increase write buffer in staging queued.
customer-ops: status updated on status.redwood.ai (note id STATUS-789). linking PD incident.
incident-bot: Alert resolved: prometheus.scrape.failure cleared (rule: prom_scrape_failures_high).
maya: closing this thread. follow-ups: 1) postmortem note with root cause (throttle on write-tier) 2) test autoscaling for write-tier under spike 3) add a scrape backoff runbook step.
ops_lead: thanks all. reassigning follow-ups to eng-ml infra for a fix.
incident-bot: Thread ended. PD incident PD-INC-98231 -> resolved.
